notes: CAUTION ON QUOTES: WebFetch returns a model-extracted summary, not the raw page. Every quote above was copied from that extraction and must be re-checked word for word against the live page by the verifier. Where the extraction was marked as a direct excerpt I used it; otherwise treat the quote as unverified.
CALL BUDGET: about 33 tool calls, over the brief's ~30 target. Eleven pages were not opened (search snippets only) and none of their facts are cited as rows. Leads are listed below.

NO ROW - Energy Fuels White Mesa Mill (Utah): the opened ColoradoBiz article (2026-07-30, https://coloradobiz.com/energy-fuels-rare-earth-plant-expansion-utah/) gives a $104 million expansion started, terbium oxide about 20 t/yr and dysprosium oxide 120 t/yr by end-2027, samarium/europium/gadolinium circuits by end-2028, and government grants and loans expected to cover much of the cost, with the current NdPr capacity at 1,000 t/yr. It says only 'Utah', not Blanding, so it cannot be a row under the city-and-state rule. Verifier: confirm the Blanding, UT city from another opened page before adding.

NO ROW - Lynas Seadrift (Texas): the opened Metal.com page (2025-11-28) says Lynas is 'unlikely to proceed with its plan to build a rare earth processing plant in Texas' and the chairman said the project 'is not expected to move forward'. It mentions the DoD up to $258 million from 2023 and says nothing of Seadrift. The Northern Miner page failed with an SSL error. Seadrift and the 2026 restructuring to a roughly $96 million oxide supply LOI (German-language aggregator, unverified) are from search snippets only.

NO ROW - Albemarle South Carolina (Chester County) lithium hydroxide plant: the search snippets name a 50,000 t/yr plant (expandable to 100,000 t/yr), but the opened Albemarle page does not mention it. Not cited.

Vulcan Elements (Benson, NC): the state incentive (about $17.5 million), the $918.1 million state figure, and the 10,000 t/yr magnet output tied to a separate $1.4 billion US government partnership come from search snippets or aggregators, not from the opened researchtriangle.org page. The Ucore 2027 oxide-delay claim is from a low-authority site and is unverified. The ncnewsline.com page returned HTTP 403.

e-VAC Magnetics (Sumter County, SC): the county is stated, not the city, so the row uses 'Sumter County' with 85 acres in the Pocotaligo Industrial Park. The schedule was late-fall 2025 production. A January 2026 aggregator (roic.ai) says it launched, but the claim is unverified. The scdailygazette.com page returned HTTP 403. Ownership by Ara Partners is from search snippets, not an opened page.

Stardust Power (Muskogee): the opened page gives no date (published null), no acreage, no capacity, no rail, power, water or reagent facts, and no former-use history. The 66-acre site and the 40-acre right of first refusal come from an SEC exhibit and search snippets, not opened pages. The 50,000 t/yr two-phase capacity is from a snippet. The page is paywalled after its lead paragraph.

Syrah Vidalia: the 45 ktpa expansion is pending a final investment decision (opened source). The Tesla offtake is 8 ktpa, about 71% of the initial 11.25 ktpa, and conditional on ramp-up and qualification. The later Reuters-cited option on another 17,000 t is from a snippet only.

Tesla Robstown: the opened article gives no nameplate capacity. The 1 million vehicles per year figure is a May 2023 Musk projection, not a capacity claim. The 50 GWh figure and the 'acid-free' process claim come from search snippets, and the fetched article makes no acid-free claim, so the two conflict. Not used.

USA Rare Earth Stillwater: the opened page is the June 2022 announcement, so status is 'announced'. Commissioning of Phase 1a in March 2026 comes from a snippet, unverified. A search snippet reports a 310,000 sq ft former Total Energy building at 100 West Airport Road, which would make the site a former-industrial reuse, but no opened page confirms it, so brownfield is null. Verifier: check this first, since it would be a brownfield fact.

MP Materials Independence: the 48C award ($58.5 million) appears on the opened page as 'received a $58.5 million award' and is recorded in doe_award with agency DOE. The 48C credit is administered by DOE with Treasury, so verify the agency wording. The 2021 GM supply agreement and the 2023 target that was missed come from snippets only.

Novonix Riverside: the opened article is the November 2021 opening, so 'operating' reflects that opening, not current production. The 2025 production target and the 2025 analyst note are from snippets. Enterprise South (second Chattanooga plant, about 31,500 t/yr) carries a conditional $754.8 million DOE loan; this is a DOE-finance lead for the DOE researcher and is not included here.

Westwater Kellyton, Alabama: no DOE loan was found. The EXIM $25 million direct loan (press release dated 2026-08-10) comes from a search snippet and I did not open the release. Phase 1 target of 12,500 mtpa is from a summary. Not included as a row. Verifier: open the release and confirm the Kellyton city and state.

Gallium/germanium DoD awards (leads, none opened): Atlantic Alumina (ATALCO), Louisiana, $150 million DoW preferred equity (Jan 2026, snippet); ReElement Technologies, Marion, Indiana, $25 million DoW (Jul 2026, snippet); Flash Metals USA (Metallium), Phase I SBIR about A$100,000 (Sep 2025, snippet) with a later Phase II about $1 million. Atlantic Alumina is the strongest brownfield-style lead for an alumina refinery.

Copper (leads, none opened): Freeport Miami smelter (AZ) expansion under evaluation (Argus, July 2025, snippet). Rio Tinto Kennecott (UT) output down after a June 2026 furnace breach (low-authority aggregator). ASARCO Hayden (AZ) idle with restart talks (Reuters 2024, snippet). No Kennecott acid-plant facts were found.

Not covered: manganese; Noveon Magnetics (San Marcos, TX) had no results in the search; Perpetua Resources' Stibnite project is in Idaho and the snippets show no link to the Thompson Falls smelter; Lynas Seadrift is a snippet-only location.
Sources not opened because of HTTP 403 (bot block): ncnewsline.com (Vulcan NC) and scdailygazette.com (e-VAC SC). Alternative pages were used for both.

Brownfield summary: Novonix (former GE turbine plant, Chattanooga) and Albemarle Kings Mountain (former lithium mine, 1,200 acres) are the two confirmed brownfield-style rows. USA Rare Earth Stillwater may also be former-industrial, but that is unconfirmed by an opened page.
